ORBIT-AI · On-orbit AI compute

An AI chip for orbit. It catches its own mistakes.

A 346 µm demonstrator that stops or repairs its own bit flips.

Demonstrator · simulated evidence · not flight-qualified

Any chip can fly. Keeping it right is the hard part.

True scale

Evidence

It catches its own mistakes, in silicon.

Four mechanisms in the routed layout. Then we flipped its bits on purpose.

M/01 DETECT

Duplicate and compare.

A mismatch stops the chip before a wrong result leaves.

M/02 REPAIR

Triple voting.

A flipped thermal copy is outvoted and rewritten next clock.

M/03 SEPARATE

Keep the twins apart.

Fences 242 µm apart; every twin ≥ 251 µm from its partner.

M/04 COMPUTE

Signed INT8 arithmetic.

Four lanes, 1.1 GOPS at 139 MHz, timing met.

Radiation

Particles hit. Bits flip.

Every protected bit is stored twice.

Twins at least 251 µm apart.

Thermal state is kept three times.

Majority vote every clock.

Where it has to work

No repair visits. No second chance.

How it compares

Built to catch its own mistakes. Nobody else shows how.

Flight processors are hardened, not AI engines. The AI chips that fly do not publish upset handling.
